what: What the Package Does (One Line, Title Case)
title: What the Package Does (One Line, Title Case)
text: ReMPCA R package designed extend Principal Component Analysis (PCA) complex, high-dimensional datasets—including curves, images, functional, regular data. integrating multiple data types within single framework, ReMPCA captures intricate relationships across variables domains, making ideal tool structured data analysis fields like imaging, signal processing, functional data analysis. Unlike traditional PCA methods, ReMPCA offers flexible, fine-grained control one- two-way regularization. Users can independently apply smoothing sparsity different data components, tailored regularization parameters across functional regular sections. Built enhanced power algorithm, package dynamically refines components quantifies explained variance, delivering powerful unified solution extracting meaningful structure hybrid datasets. Implementing varied penalties uu vv improves accuracy. shown Figure , noisy chessboard, applying power algorithm customized penalties, smoothness group lasso, enforces step-function structure uu vv, refining vectors yielding reconstruction close true chessboard. importantly, regularizing directions simultaneously effective separate one-way penalties, better preserving data’s true structure. gwid pipeline

title: What the Package Does (One Line, Title Case)
text: following example demonstrates generate q hybrid data (regular functional) construct input objects required running ReMPCA:
code: library(ReMPCA) set.seed(123)  # Create a common left singular vector u (length 150), with sparsity in the first half x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 150) u <- sin(x) u[1:75] <- 0  ### Construct 4 variables with different characteristics  # Variable 1: Sparse right singular vector m1 <- 20 v1 <- rnorm(m1, sd = 0.8) v1[sample(1:m1, 5)] <- v1[sample(1:m1, 5)] * 1e-2 + rnorm(5, sd = 0.01) X1 <- outer(u, v1) + rnorm(150 * m1, sd = 0.03)  # Variable 2: Piecewise smooth right singular vector (functional) x2 <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 40) v2 <- cos(2 * x2) v2[21:40] <- 0  # Create piecewise structure X2 <- outer(u, v2) + rnorm(150 * 40, sd = 0.5)  # Variable 3: Smooth right singular vector (functional) m3 <- 30 x3 <- seq(0, pi, length.out = m3) v3 <- sin(x3) X3 <- outer(u, v3) + rnorm(150 * m3, sd = 0.2)  # Variable 4: Random structure m4 <- 10 v4 <- rnorm(m4) X4 <- outer(u, v4) + rnorm(150 * m4, sd = 0.05)  # Combine all variables into a single matrix (optional, not used directly) X <- cbind(X1, X2, X3, X4)  ### Create hybrid data objects  # Regular data (RD) object rd_object1 <- rdClass(   data = as.matrix(X1),   Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(1, 19, length.out = 10)) )  # Functional data (FD) objects fd_object2 <- fdClass(   data = as.matrix(X2),   argval = NULL,   Smoothing_parameter = NULL,   Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0, 39, length.out = 20)) )  fd_object3 <- fdClass(   data = as.matrix(X3),   argval = NULL,   Smoothing_parameter = NULL,   Sparsity_parameter = 0 )  # Another regular data object rd_object4 <- rdClass(   data = as.matrix(X4),   Sparsity_parameter = 0 )  # Combine all objects into a hybrid data structure hd_list <- list(rd_object1, fd_object2, fd_object3, rd_object4) object_list <- hdClass(   hdlist = hd_list,   argval = NULL,   Smoothing_parameter = NULL,   Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0, 149, length.out = 20)) )  # Plot the data par(mfrow = c(2, 4), pin = c(1, 1), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 2), pty = "s")  # Variable 1: Regular matplot(v1, type = 'p', pch = 16, main = 'v1, Regular')  abline(h = 0, col = 'red', lty = 2) image(t(X1), main = 'X1, Regular')  # Variable 2: Functional matplot(svd(X2)$v[,1], type = 'l', main = 'v2, Functional')  abline(h = 0, col = 'red', lty = 2) image(t(X2), main = 'X2, Functional')  # Variable 3: Functional matplot(svd(X3)$v[,1], type = 'l', main = 'v3, Functional') image(t(X3), main = 'X3, Functional')  # Variable 4: Regular matplot(v4, type = 'p', pch = 16, main = 'v4, Regular') image(t(X4), main = 'X4, Regular')

title: ReMPCA Smooth and Sparse Multivariate Functional Principal Component Analysis — ReMPCA
text: hd hdClass object. centerhds logical; True, demeans data calculating principal components. num_pcs integer. number principal components. nfolds_u integer. used cross validation approach tuning level sparsity rows. nfolds_v integer vector length p (number variables), -th element specifies number cross-validation folds use -th variable. provided (NULL), value 5 assigned variables default. thresh convergence threshold power algorithm. maxit Maximum number iterations power algorithm. tuning_iter Integer specifying number iterations perform tuning process conditional smoothing sparsity parameters. parallel Logical; TRUE, parallel computation used fit models across different sparsity parameter values. Users must register parallel backend beforehand using packages doParallel, doMC, similar. weights Optional numeric vector scaling weights. NULL, function automatically computes weights based inverse square root average variance variable. set 0, scaling applied. numeric vector provided, length must match number variables, element used scale corresponding variable. used adjust scale differences across variables hybrid data object. smoothness_type character string specifying method used smoothing u /v, must one "Second_order" (default), "First_order" "Indicator". sparse_tuning_type character string specifying sparse calculation method. Must one "soft" (default), "hard", "SCAD". tuning_order character string representing tuning order. set 'Sparsity', sparsity parameters tuned first, followed smoothness. set 'Smoothness', order reversed. cv.pick character string specifying rule used select optimal tuning parameter cross-validation sparsity. set 'min', tuning parameter corresponding minimum cross-validation error chosen. set '1se' (default), 1-standard-error rule applied, selecting regularized model whose error within one standard error minimum. sparse_tuning_u Optional. Specifies sparsity level(s) rows: single non-negative integer fixed sparsity. numeric vector candidate values, selected via cross-validation (CV). Set 0 sparsity. NULL, function defaults Sparsity_parameter attribute hdClass object. sparse_tuning_v Optional. list length p (number variables), -th element either numeric value vector specifying candidate sparsity levels -th variable. set NULL, function default using Sparsity_parameter_col attribute input object class hdClass. smooth_tuning_u Optional. Specifies smoothing parameter rows: single number fixed smoothness. numeric vector candidate values, selected via generalized cross-validation (GCV). Set 0 smoothness NULL, function defaults Smoothing_parameter attribute hdClass object. smooth_tuning_v Optional. list length p (number variables), -th element either numeric value vector specifying candidate smoothing parameters -th variable. set NULL, function default using Smoothing_parameter_col attribute input object class hdClass.

title: Hybrid Data Constructor (hdClass) — hdClass
text: hdClass S3 class representing hybrid data, consisting list functional (fdClass), raw (rdClass), image (imgClass) data objects. input list (hdlist) can contain mix fdClass, rdClass, imgClass objects. objects must number observations (.e., number rows). Image objects (imgClass) interpreted either functional raw based internal class inheritance. resulting object matrix column-wise concatenation input matrices includes following attributes: GridPoints_u: Row grid points. Smoothing_parameter: Row smoothing parameter(s). Sparsity_parameter: Row sparsity parameter(s). n_var: Number variables (.e., number objects hdlist). ncol: Number columns variable. Smoothing_parameter_col: List smoothing parameters variable. Sparsity_parameter_col: List sparsity parameters variable. GridPoints_v: List grid points (columns) variable. variable_types: Character vector type labels variable: "hd" (functional) "rd" (raw).
